subject: maths
question: If two circles of radii 35 cm and 25 cm touch each other externally, then the length (in cm) of a common tangent is (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two circles with radii **R** and **r** touch each other **externally**, the length of their **Direct Common Tangent** is given by the formula:

Length = 2 × √(R × r)

Given: **R = 35 cm** and **r = 25 cm**.

⇒ Length = 2 × √(35 × 25) = 2 × 5 × √35

⇒ Length = 10 × 5.916 = 59.16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 59.16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of first circle (R₁) = 35 cm

Radius of second circle (R₂) = 25 cm

Condition: Circles touch **externally**.

**Formula Used:**

1. Distance between centers (d) = R₁ + R₂ (for external touch)

2. Length of Direct Common Tangent (L) = √[d² − (R₁ − R₂)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40dda8d1dff72ec95b01e195b2d27a29ea3084c8b5fc52af578fb43ed234e028.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance between centers (d) = 35 + 25 = 60 cm

⇒ L = √[60² − (35 − 25)²]

⇒ L = √[3600 − 10²]

⇒ L = √[3600 − 100]

⇒ L = √3500

⇒ L = 59.16079... ≈ 59.16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 59.16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length of a transverse common tangent is √[d² − (R₁ + R₂)²]. For circles touching externally, TCT length is zero.

Internal Touch Condition

If two circles touch internally, the distance between their centers (d) is equal to |R₁ − R₂|.

Number of Common Tangents

When circles touch externally, there are exactly 3 common tangents (2 direct and 1 transverse).</p
